# NSSFactory r2 — Wolf 359

_Farther out, seen more clearly._

A VapourSynth factory for classical NSS (non-local self-similarity) denoisers — NLM, BM3D (+VAggregate), BM4D, WNNM, MCWNNM, TWSC, NLH, NCSR, LSSC, and DA3D on top of them — honoring the pre-AI era of these algorithms, on the CPU (`nss`) and on NVIDIA GPUs (`nss_cuda`). r2 adds two filters, BM4D and DA3D, sharpens the models where r1 lost detail, makes the slowest GPU filters faster, and documents what each filter's `sigma` really means.

**Work in progress.** The packages below are preview builds for evaluation, not stable releases.

## Packages

| Package | Plugin | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `nssfactory-r2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2; glibc 2.34 and the libstdc++ of GCC 13 (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39 or later). Highway dynamic: AVX2 + AVX3/Zen4 |
| `nssfactory-r2-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | AArch64 with glibc 2.38 (libstdc++ built in). NEON |
| `nssfactory-r2-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.dylib` (`nss`) | Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or newer. NEON |
| `nssfactory-r2-windows-x86_64.zip` | `libnss.dll` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2 and the Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable |
| `nssfactory-r2-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | `libnss_cuda.so` (`nss_cuda`) | as `linux-x86_64`, with an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 12.9 or newer |
| `nssfactory-r2-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip` | `libnss_cuda.dll` (`nss_cuda`) | an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 12.9 or newer and the Visual C++ Redistributable |

Clips must be constant-format Gray/YUV/RGB 32-bit float. BM4D and DA3D are in `nss` only; `nss_cuda` has the other filters. Each package carries `docs/api`: the [API guide](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/README.md), the [CUDA reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md) and the new [comparison with other plugins](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/compare.md). `core.nss.Version()` and `core.nss_cuda.Version()` report `r2`.

## Highlights

- **New: `nss.DA3D(clip, ref, sigma)`**, data-adaptive dual-domain denoising (Pierazzo and Facciolo, IPOL 2017): a last step on another denoiser's output. Over a BM3D guide on 9 anime frames: +0.75 / +1.3 / +2.2 dB (gray) and +0.9 / +1.9 / +3.4 dB (RGB) at sigma 5 / 10 / 25; little at sigma 2. Matches the authors' reference implementation to 0.001 dB with the same tiles, and gives the same bits on every SIMD target. CPU only.
- **New: `nss.BM4D(clip, sigma)`**, block matching and 4D filtering (Maggioni et al., TIP 2013) with the clip as a volume, written from the paper with the authors' default parameters. Against temporal BM3D on an anime episode it wins 9 of 12 segments (+0.2 to +6 dB on still, slow and panning scenes) and loses 0.15 to 1.3 dB in fast action. Heavy: 1.2 fps for 1080p gray on 16 threads. CPU only.
- **LSSC model 4: text and fine detail kept.** Every patch is now coded on its own by error-constrained orthogonal matching pursuit instead of r1's cluster soft threshold, which dimmed white text by 4 levels at sigma 3 and by about 21 at sigma 15. On 11 test images: +1.9 / +1.3 / +0.8 dB at sigma 3 / 10 / 25 against model 3, no image below its noisy input at sigma 3 (model 3: 8 of 11), white text within 0.2 levels at sigma 3. The default `block_step` is now `block_size / 2`.
- **NLH model 7: a better blind estimate.** The blind noise estimate read Gaussian chroma noise 1.41x high; it is now corrected. Blind NLH gains +0.2 to +1.0 dB on RGB, YUV444 and YUV420 at sigma 2 to 25, on every test image.
- **BM3D searches a wider window by default** (`bm_range` 7 → 9): +0.06 to +0.14 dB.
- **Faster where it was slowest** (1080p defaults, RTX 5080, against r1 with the same toolkit): LSSC 1.28x (YUV420) / 1.18x (RGB), TWSC 1.15x / 1.25x, temporal BM3D 1.13x and temporal WNNM 1.18x at `radius=1`; the other filters keep r1's speed.
- **Tensor cores for large search windows.** BM3D, WNNM and NCSR with `bm_range` 20 or more, and TWSC, match on FP16 tensor cores with an exact re-rank: the same matches bit for bit, BM3D `bm_range=30` 1.6x, TWSC 1.2–1.3x (RTX 30 series and newer).
- **CPU:** LSSC codes six patches per pass of its dictionary product, bit for bit as before: 1.18x at 1080p on 16 cores, 1.2–1.4x on one.
- **Compared in the open.** The new [comparison page](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/compare.md) runs `nss` and `nss_cuda` against BM3DCUDA, bm3dcpu, VapourSynth-WNNM, vs-nlm-ispc and vs-nlm-cuda on the same input with the same arguments: the same output at the same arguments, +0.93 dB (BM3D) and +0.33 dB (WNNM) with `radius=1`, and on the GPU 1.35x BM3DCUDA (2.8x for both stages, 2.5x temporal), 1.6–3.0x vs-nlm-cuda, and WNNM at 19x the CPU-only VapourSynth-WNNM.
- **What `sigma` means, per filter.** At the default settings only LSSC and NLH want the noise's true sigma; BM3D wants about 4/3 of it, NCSR 1.8, WNNM 2.2, MCWNNM 2.5, TWSC 3.4, and NLM an `h` of 0.6 to 0.8 sigma. Measured on anime frames from sigma 1 to 20 and documented on every page ([Sigma at the default settings](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md#sigma-at-the-default-settings)); the arguments themselves are unchanged.
- **Smaller CUDA packages**: the device code is compressed (about 90 → 20 MB of fat binary).

## Upgrading from r1

- **Model versions changed:** LSSC 2 → 4, NLH 6 → 7, and NCSR 2 → 3 for anyone still on the original r1 assets (the r1 assets were refreshed with NCSR 3 on 2026-10-18). Their output changes; legacy temporal intermediates carry the version and must be recomputed (`VAggregate` rejects mixed versions).
- **Defaults changed:** LSSC `block_step` 8 → `block_size / 2`; BM3D `bm_range` 7 → 9. Pass the old values to keep r1's geometry (the LSSC model itself still differs).
- **NLH with `rclip`:** give a prefiltered clip. Since model 7, a plane matched on another has its blind estimate scaled down; the noisy clip itself as `rclip` reads its luma noise too low.
- NLM, WNNM, MCWNNM, TWSC, and NCSR against the refreshed r1 assets, gave r1's output bit for bit at their defaults in our checks (1080p YUV420 and RGB).

## Known limits

- BM4D and DA3D have no GPU version yet (planned for r3). Both take the noise's true sigma and assume white Gaussian noise.
- Speeds are measured on one RTX 5080 with a Ryzen 9 5950X; other GPUs are untested for speed.
- The CUDA packages are built with CUDA 12.9 for driver compatibility. A CUDA 13 build runs NLM about 1.35x faster at its defaults (same output); every other filter is within 4%. The documented speeds are the release build's.
- NLH's blind estimate still reads textured luma high at very low noise (sigma 5 or less); give `sigma` there when it is known.
